chunks: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Abbas said, and he ascribed it (to the Prophet or Imam), saying:

Muawiya asked Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) about manliness (al-muru'ah), so he said: A man's avariciousness towards his religion, his rectification of his property, and his establishment of rights. Muawiya said: You did well, O Abu Muhammad! You did well, O Abu Muhammad! He said: Muawiya then used to say after that: I had wished that Yazid said it, and indeed he was half-blinded.

key_terms.إِصْلَاح الْمَال: Rectification or proper management of wealth
key_terms.الْمُرُوءَة: Manliness, virtue, or nobility of character
key_terms.شُحّ: Avarice, stinginess, or hoarding (here used positively as guarding one's religion)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of manliness (al-muru'ah) according to Imam Hasan in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Muawiya’s pragmatic inquiry into 'manliness' is answered by Imam al-Hasan with a triad of spiritual and social integrity: guarding one’s faith, managing wealth responsibly, and fulfilling rights. Muawiya’s immediate praise and subsequent wish that his son Yazid possessed this moral depth—despite his physical defect of being half-blinded (*a’war*)—highlights the Shia emphasis on inner virtue over external appearance or political power.
